facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
Mr Ter-Petrosyan announced that the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election had not been free and fair.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the daily protest rallies from 20 February 2008 onwards was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed at Freedom Square and the surrounding area around the clock, having set up a camp.
The applicant was an active participant in the rallies at Freedom Square, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins from 20 February 2008 onwards.
The applicant contested the Government's allegations and submitted that the assembly at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 had been peaceful and none of the demonstrators had been armed.
The applicant submitted that it was the police who had attacked the peaceful demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, using excessive force, in order to terminate the assembly.
On 1 March 2008, apparently at some point between 6 and 7 a.m., police forces arrived on Freedom Square in Yerevan.

The Government alleged that the purpose of the 1 March 2008 police operation at Freedom Square was the verification of information obtained by the police a day earlier, according to which the demonstrators possessed arms and ammunition.
The Government alleged that the members of the police force who arrived at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 were not equipped with any protective gear.
The Government alleged that hundreds of demonstrators armed with metal rods and wooden clubs had gathered at Freedom Square, waiting for the police officers.
The Government alleged that the demonstrators attacked the police officers at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, hitting them and throwing stones, pointed metal objects and Molotov cocktails at them.
The Government alleged that numerous police officers were injured as a result of the demonstrators' attack at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008.
The applicant was present at Freedom Square when the police operation was conducted on 1 March 2008.
The applicant submitted that it was the police who had attacked the peaceful demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, using excessive force, in order to terminate the assembly.
As a result of the police operation on 1 March 2008, all the demonstrators present at Freedom Square, including the applicant, fled from the square.

According to the record of the applicant's bringing-in drafted by arresting police officers H.K. and E.K., the applicant was brought in to Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station from Freedom Square at 8.50 a.m. on 1 March 2008 on suspicion of having put up resistance to a police officer.

Police officer H.K. reported in writing to the chief of Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station that the applicant had been brought in from Freedom Square for having put up resistance by disobeying their lawful orders, refusing to be taken to the police station, pushing them and trying to flee.

Police officer E.K. reported in writing to the chief of Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station that the applicant had been brought in from Freedom Square for having put up resistance by disobeying their lawful orders, refusing to be taken to the police station, pushing them and trying to flee.
The applicant was questioned as a witness and stated that he had continuously participated in the demonstrations at Freedom Square.
The applicant stated that on 1 March 2008, early in the morning, police forces had arrived at Freedom Square and started violently dispersing the demonstrators gathered there.

The applicant stated that he had tried to persuade the police officers not to apply force at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, but had been attacked with tear gas and batons and had been pushed to the ground.

The decision instituting criminal case no. 62202608 stated that a number of demonstrators had illegally carried arms and ammunition and committed life- and health-threatening assault on police officers.

Police officer H.K. stated that, having been given the task of pursuing and finding persons who had fled Freedom Square, he had stopped one man who was walking with a few others for an identity check at the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street on 1 March 2008.

Police officer H.K. stated that the man he stopped at the intersection of Northern Avenue and Abovyan Street had been calm at first, but after being asked to follow him to a police station to check whether he had been involved in the unlawful events at Freedom Square, the man had pushed him and tried to flee.

Police officer H.K. stated that police officer E.K. had approached at that moment, and the man had pushed police officer E.K. as well, but then the man had surrendered to the officers and had been taken to Kanaker-Zeytun Police Station where he had been identified as the applicant.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that on 1 March 2008 at around 7 a.m., when police officers demanded the demonstrators gathered at Freedom Square to give them a possibility to verify the veracity of the information that the demonstrators possessed arms and ammunition and once again warned them to end the unlawful event, the applicant disobeyed the lawful orders of police officers H.K. and E.K. and assaulted them in a non-life or health-threatening way by pushing and pulling them.
In reaching its findings, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan relied on the statements of police officers H.K. and E.K.

The applicant stated that he had tried to persuade the police officers not to apply force at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008, but had been attacked with tear gas and batons and had been pushed to the ground.

According to the applicant, he had been unable to question properly the police officers H.K. and E.K. in court as the trial judge disallowed some of the questions, namely those related to the lawfulness of the police actions at Freedom Square in the morning of 1 March 2008, as not related to the circumstances of the case under examination.
